cases.name: Lindsay Elizabeth Daum
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Lindsay graduated from Niwot High School in 2000 and obtained her bachelor’s degree in Psychology from the University of Maryland. Lindsay married Gabriel Jay Sinner in 2003. Gabriel was on active duty in the US Navy, and he and Lindsay moved to Yokosuka, Japan where he was stationed. They had 3 three children together while he was stationed in Japan, until he was transferred to San Diego in 2010. Lindsay’s family was so happy to have her and the kids back stateside, finally just a short flight away. Gabriel and Lindsay parted ways in 2015. Lindsay returned to Colorado and Gabriel continued his career at sea.

Shortly after returning to Colorado, she began working for the Department of Revenue in the Division of Motor Vehicles. Always a dedicated hard worker, Lindsay was so proud to be able to buy a new home for her children, first in Frederick, and then a brand new one in Loveland in 2018. She loved being a mom more than anything else and loved spending time with her kids and taking them out on adventures, and chose to work from home so she could be close to her kids. She also loved animals all of her life. Her 5 dogs and 3 cats were proof she would take in any animal that needed a home. Also a faithful Christian, she attended Flatiron’s Christian Church in Longmont regularly."

cases.name: Meadow Lily Sinner
cases.about:
Her Go Fund Me said, "Meadow was only 16 and one of the most beautiful and vibrant souls we have ever met. She was a leader in the Colorado Youth Congress and was working with her peers to improve mental health support in schools. Inside CYC, Meadow held the role of community builder — she was the one we trusted to begin all of our meetings because her charisma and humor were so infectious. She had the power to transform the energy of a room in a matter of seconds, and that’s one of the many reasons we loved her so deeply. Meadow was also brave, vulnerable, and deeply in love with her family and her community. Her death will leave an irreparable hole in the hearts of all that knew and loved her."

Her obituary said, "She was going to be a Junior at Mountain View High School in Loveland, Colorado. She was a beautiful, vibrant soul and the life of the party. She was a leader in the Colorado Youth Congress and was working with her peers to improve mental health support in schools. Inside CYC, she held the role of community builder. She was known to have an infectious charisma, fantastic sense of humor, and a flair for drama. She loved to be on stage and in the spotlight. She performed in Clue, Seussical the Musical, and sadly passed a few short days before performing in the Rocky Horror Picture Show with the Harrington Arts Alliance at The Lincoln Center in Fort Collins, one of the region's premier venues. She was the picture of joy to her friends, family and a cherished granddaughter, sister, and niece.

Meadow was the definition of a big sister to her siblings. She would have done anything to protect them. Her siblings loved being around her and she spent hours with them giving advice and entertaining them. Meadow was a people person and touched the life of anyone and everyone she met. She had a countless number of friends whom she loved and cared for."
